When the world changes, a company must know what to do.
=======================================================

Simdots simulates a shock on a business and returns the next moves: prices, banks, stock, alternative suppliers and purchasing.

Problem
-------

Tariffs, wars and headlines move overnight, and smaller companies react by instinct. In our interviews a tannery decides "by nose", an optics company "by feel", and a construction company pays consultants for the answer. Knowing the loss is not enough. They need the next move.

Solution
--------

1.  Map the business in 10 minutes.
2.  A tariff, a war or a statement from a president hits.
3.  Thousands of simulations combine macro data, trends and global logistics to show the loss.
4.  The plan ranks each move by the margin it protects.

Backtests and progress
----------------------

**−1.2 pts**average gap from reality on the Hormuz, Ukraine and Crimea benchmarks (internal)

**2**companies paid about €1k each for analysis from our engine, through our consultancy

**1k**users on our data tools, datastripes.com and howtocsv.com. The app is live

Market
------

$2.4B global supply chain risk software market, growing ~12% a year. SAM of €560M: 311k EU manufacturers with 10–249 employees at €1,800/year. Three-year target: 1,000 customers, €1.8M.

Business model
--------------

Pro at €1,800 a year, custom plans for consultants and larger firms. Simulations run on the customer's computer, so serving a new customer costs us almost nothing.

Landscape
---------

Resilinc, Everstream and Interos sell enterprise contracts that take months to deploy. Kpler, Panjiva and Sayari sell trade data. Consultants work per project. Simdots is self-serve, and supplier data stays on the device.
